title: Iterative Prompting: Asking AI to Improve Its Own Output
introduction: In this lesson you will learn how to work with an AI step by step, review its first answer, point out problems, and ask for a better version. This skill helps you get clearer, more useful results.

sections.heading: Understanding Iterative Prompting
sections.subheading: Why a single prompt may not be enough
paragraphs: Iterative prompting means you talk to the AI more than once. First you ask a question, then you look at the answer, and you ask again to fix any issues.
Each round lets you guide the AI toward the exact result you need.

example.title: First Prompt and Follow‑up
example.content: You ask: “Write a short story about a cat.” The AI replies. You then say: “Add a surprise ending where the cat solves a mystery.” The AI gives a revised story.

sections.heading: Spotting Weaknesses in the AI’s First Output
sections.subheading: How to notice missing details or errors
paragraphs: Read the AI’s reply carefully. Look for unclear parts, missing information, or facts that don’t make sense.
Mark the exact spots that need change before you ask for a revision.

example.title: Missing Detail Example
example.content: The AI writes a recipe for pancakes but forgets to mention cooking time. You note: “The recipe does not say how long to cook each side.”

sections.heading: Giving Clear, Targeted Feedback
sections.subheading: Specific instructions lead to better revisions
paragraphs: Instead of saying “make it better,” tell the AI exactly what to change: add, remove, shorten, or re‑phrase.
Use phrases like “please include …”, “make the tone more friendly”, or “reduce the length to three sentences.”

example.title: Specific Feedback Example
example.content: You say: “Please add a line that explains why the cat loves fish, and keep the story under 150 words.” The AI updates the story accordingly.

sections.heading: Comparing Versions and Trusting Your Judgment
sections.subheading: Choose the best result and remember AI can err
paragraphs: After each revision, compare the new answer with the previous one. Keep the version that best meets your goal.
Even when the AI critiques its own work, its assessment may be wrong. Always verify facts yourself.

example.title: Version Comparison Example
example.content: Version 1 describes the cat’s mystery in detail. Version 2 shortens the mystery but adds an inaccurate fact about cats being nocturnal. You select Version 1 and correct the mistake yourself.

practice.title: Try an Iterative Prompt
practice.instruction: Write a short prompt asking the AI to list three benefits of walking. Read the answer, then write one sentence telling the AI to add a short example for each benefit. Imagine the AI’s revised list.

keyTakeaways: Iterative prompting lets you improve AI answers by reviewing and asking again.
Identify exact weaknesses before giving feedback.
Clear, specific instructions produce better revisions.
Always compare versions and double‑check AI’s self‑critique.

mcqs.question: What does the term "iterative prompting" mean in the lesson?
options: Giving a single instruction and stopping.
Talking to the AI in multiple rounds, reviewing and revising.
Providing the AI with a list of unrelated topics.
Letting the AI generate answers without any user input.
mcqs.explanation: Iterative prompting involves asking the AI, checking its answer, and then asking again to improve the result.

mcqs.question: Before you ask the AI for a revision, the lesson advises you to:
options: Guess what might be wrong.
Read the AI’s reply carefully and note the exact spots that need change.
Immediately ask for a longer answer.
Change the topic entirely.
mcqs.explanation: You should examine the first output, identify missing details or errors, and mark where changes are needed.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of clear, targeted feedback?
options: Make it better.
Add more details.
Please include a line explaining why the cat loves fish, and keep the story under 150 words.
Rewrite everything.
mcqs.explanation: Specific instructions like adding a line and setting a word limit give the AI precise guidance.

mcqs.question: When comparing two revised versions, what is an essential practice?
options: Choose the longer version automatically.
Trust the AI’s self‑critique without checking.
Verify facts yourself and select the version that best meets your goal.
Ignore any differences and pick randomly.
mcqs.explanation: The lesson stresses that you must double‑check facts and decide which version best satisfies your requirements.

mcqs.question: In the practice activity, after receiving a list of three benefits of walking, the next step is to:
options: Ask the AI to add a short example for each benefit.
Delete the list and start over.
Request a poem about running instead.
Ask for the benefits in a different language.
mcqs.explanation: The exercise tells you to write a sentence telling the AI to add a short example for each benefit.
